name: Shankh (Shankha) Bhasma

sections.overview: Shankh (Shankha) Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction:
Shankha Bhasma is an Ayurvedic preparation from Conch shell which is a powder of a substance obtained by calcination. It balances Vata and Pitta Dosha It is useful excellent Ayurvedic remedy for digestive system complaints like gastritis, abdominal pain, malabsorption syndrome etc. This Bhasma has properties to improve digestion, absorbs excess liquid content, improves appetite and cures gastritis, acidity, nausea etc. 
 Do you know about Shankha? 
 It is a soft body organism that lives inside dense, very hard and calcareous shell or conch. Shankha is also known as “Indian conch”. Two types of Shankha is available one is called Vama varta (opening of this shankha is on left side) and Dakshin varta (opening of this shankha is on right side). For medicinal preparation “Vama varta” shankha is used. 
 Different names of Shankha: 

 Sanskrit name: Shankha 
 English name: Conch shell 
 Hindi name: Shankh 
 Kannada name: Shankha 
 Gujarati name: Shankh 
 Malayalam name: Shankham
sections.ingredients:

 Aloe vera juice or lemon juice

 Preparation of this Bhasma is by use of purified Conch shell. There are various different techniques for its preparation. Any method can be used. Here is one of the process.

This then dried and burnt in the absence of air, at a temperature of 800 – 900 degree Celsius and then it is allowed for self-cooling. This process is repeated twice to obtain bhasma.

sections.therapeutic_uses:

 Aloe vera juice or lemon juice

 Medicinal Properties

 Veerya (Potency): Sheeta (Cold)

 Irritable bowel syndrome 
 Flatulence

 Gastritis

 Asthma 
 Lung diseases 
 Bronchitis 
 Jaundice 
 
 Contraindication 
 
 Self-medication can prove risky. 
 Have this medicine in accurate dose and for restrictedperiod of time, as suggested by doctor. 
 Keep out of the reach and sight of children. 
 Store it in a dry and cool place. 
 Avoid inconstipation problem. 
 This Bhasma isalso contraindicated in cracked skin & fissures. 
 
 Dosage 
 Take 250 mg – 500 mg of Bhasma once or twice daily before or after having food or as recommended by Ayurvedic doctor. 
 Traditional administration was along with honey, lemon juice, and triphala kashaya etc.
